name: Steel Pink
lede: Steel Pink is a vivid magenta named for a mineral or metal word, "steel," despite looking nothing like the grey metal itself.

sections.title: A metal word on a magenta
sections.body: The nearest named colors on file are [[pinky-purple]], [[medium-orchid]], [[byzantine]] and [[phlox]], at 4.2, 5.2, 6.8 and 6.9 ΔE [1]. The sources we hold do not explain why a bright magenta carries a metal's name; no recipe or alloy connects the two here [1]. At lightness 51 and chroma 88, it reads as one of the most saturated colors anywhere in our library, closer to a pure dye than to anything grey [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive of 23,781 paintings, as photographed, has no painting where this magenta covers five percent or more of the canvas within six CIEDE2000 units [2]. Pigments and dyes this saturated and this pink-purple are rare in painted canvases of any period; the color belongs more to modern synthetic dye and print than to the historical palette [2].

origin.named_after: the metal word "steel"; the connection to this magenta is undocumented
origin.first_recorded: undocumented in the sources we hold
